name: How the Dambana is drawn
description: The Dambana in this game is a general representation, not a copy of any community's shrine: a small shrine raised on thin bamboo poles, with a thatched roof, a hanging fringe of dried grass and small offerings of rice and a leaf bundle. Spanish-era writers describe small raised shrines and offering places for the anito, called by names such as pinag-anituhan among the Tagalog; their exact forms varied from place to place and are not well documented. This drawing is the same for every tradition and waits for a historian's review; designs for each tradition will come only with sources.
tradition: Widespread (generic form inspired by raised bamboo shrines)
sources: William Henry Scott, Barangay: Sixteenth-Century Philippine Culture and Society (Ateneo de Manila University Press, 1994)
Juan de Plasencia, Customs of the Tagalogs (1589), in Blair and Robertson, The Philippine Islands, vol. 7
